topics.why_in_news: India and Russia held a high-level round table to strengthen cooperation in steel sector focusing on raw materials, technology transfer, industrial collaboration and supply-chain resilience.
prelims_quick_notes: India aims to achieve 300 million tonnes steel capacity by 2030.
Russia is major supplier of coking coal and mineral resources.
Cooperation focuses on steel production, raw materials and technology sharing.
Supports India’s Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India initiatives.
Focus on advanced metallurgy and green steel technologies.
Steel sector critical for infrastructure and industrial growth.
India seeks diversified and resilient supply chains.
important_facts: Coking coal is essential for steel production.
India heavily depends on imports for coking coal.
Joint R&D proposed for sustainable steel production.
India targets 300 million tonnes steel production capacity by 2030.
Cooperation includes equipment manufacturing and technology transfer.
key_highlights: Round table held between Ministry of Steel and Russian counterparts.
Focus on raw material sourcing and technology collaboration.
Discussion on joint research and industrial cooperation.
Supply-chain diversification and strategic resource security emphasised.
Green steel and sustainable production technologies discussed.
exam_relevance: Important for International Relations, Economy and Industrial Policy.
Useful for resource security, supply chains and core industries topics.
Can be linked with Indo-Russia relations and strategic economic diplomacy.
prelims_traps: Coking coal differs from thermal coal.
India still depends significantly on imports for coking coal.
India–Russia ties extend beyond defence and energy sectors.
